title: Finding useful information
goal: Compare search strategies while preserving source and access information.
case: Five fictional college policies must answer student questions.
terms: A short passage from a larger source; keep its document ID and version.
Matches terms in a query and passage; useful when wording overlaps.
Compares numerical representations of text; a production embedding model can capture semantic similarity.
Only retrieve passages that the current role is allowed to read.
steps: Create a five-policy corpus with access labels
Search ten questions with token overlap
Use the supplied synonym expansion as a meaning-aware proxy
Measure whether the known policy is in the top two
example: P2 says library loans may be extended once.
Question uses the phrase renew a book.
Exact overlap may miss P2; a simple synonym mapping improves this case but can create other misses.
misconception: The synonym mapping is a production embedding model.
correction: It is an inspectable proxy for class discussion. A vector index would require a tested embedding model.
change: Remove a synonym or lower top-k from 2 to 1 and compare recall.
lab: Compare token overlap and the synonym proxy on a fixed corpus.
output: Corpus manifest and retrieval misses with evidence IDs.
